problems: high-cardinality group fields: ParentImage (1 distinct / 1 rows), User (1 distinct / 1 rows)

findings.detail: The final exclusion whitelists User CORP\jdoe or CORP\asmith when ParentImage is Office16 WINWORD/EXCEL, IntegrityLevel=Medium, and CommandLine lacks the plaintext keywords (-w hidden|-nop|-noprofile|bypass|downloadstring|iex|frombase64string|http). But attack_step 2 is an -enc/-EncodedCommand base64 payload, where ALL of those keywords live inside the base64 blob, not the visible command line. So any attacker running (or compromising the token of) jdoe/asmith who spawns powershell -enc from a macro in Office16 Word/Excel at Medium integrity is fully excluded - exactly the primary attack this rule is meant to catch. The exclusion negates the detection.
findings.fix_hint: Do not whitelist encoded-command executions. Remove -enc activity from any benign-user allowlist, or require the allowlist to also prove the base64 decodes to an approved script; the keyword NOT-match is meaningless against -EncodedCommand.

findings.detail: Image is pinned to the exact path C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe. The 32-bit copy at C:\Windows\SysWOW64\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe is a legitimate, always-present powershell.exe that satisfies attack_step 2 but does not match this literal path, so the search misses it entirely.
findings.fix_hint: Match on Image="*\\powershell.exe" (or OriginalFileName=PowerShell.EXE) instead of a single absolute path, covering System32 and SysWOW64.

findings.detail: The regex alternation (enc|encodedcommand|ec|e) only matches those exact tokens followed by whitespace. PowerShell accepts any unambiguous prefix of -EncodedCommand, so -en, -enco, -encod, -encode, -encoded, -encodedc, -encodedcomman all work but are NOT matched (after 'enc' the next char 'o/d/e' is not \s). Attacker uses 'powershell -encoded <base64>' and evades.
findings.fix_hint: Match the prefix family explicitly, e.g. (?i)\s-(e|ec|en|enc|enco|encod|encode|encoded|encodedc|encodedco|encodedcom|encodedcomm|encodedcomma|encodedcomman|encodedcommand)\b or use -e[ncodeam]* ... with a word boundary/separator class.

findings.detail: The regex requires \s+ between the switch and the base64 (-enc<space>B64). PowerShell also accepts a colon separator, e.g. -EncodedCommand:<base64> or -enc:<base64>, which has no whitespace and is not matched.
findings.fix_hint: Allow the separator to be whitespace OR colon: ...-(enc|...)[\s:]+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}.

findings.detail: The exclusion hardcodes the Office16 click-to-run path (...\root\Office16\(WINWORD|EXCEL).EXE). Office version/channel changes (Office15, Office19, msi install path C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Office\...) would break the intended benign-user allowlist, causing it to no longer apply - noise rather than evasion, but the pinned version is fragile.
findings.fix_hint: Use a version-agnostic pattern such as *\\Microsoft Office\\*\\(WINWORD|EXCEL).EXE for the exclusion parent match.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS01.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>"C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" -enc SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQA</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE" /n</Data><Data Name='IntegrityLevel'>Medium</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Primary attack path, but User=CORP\jdoe + Office16 WINWORD + Medium integrity + no plaintext bad keyword (all payload is in the base64) satisfies the final NOT-exclusion, so the search drops it. Demonstrates the critical whitelist defeat.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS01.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\SysWOW64\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>"C:\Windows\SysWOW64\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" -enc SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQA</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\bwayne</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE" /n</Data><Data Name='IntegrityLevel'>Medium</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Legit 32-bit PowerShell at SysWOW64 path; Image!= the hardcoded System32 path so the search never matches despite being the exact attack behavior.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS02.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>"C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" -encoded SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQA</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\bwayne</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\EXCEL.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\EXCEL.EXE"</Data><Data Name='IntegrityLevel'>Medium</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: PowerShell accepts -encoded as a valid prefix of -EncodedCommand, but the regex alternation (enc|encodedcommand|ec|e)\s+ fails because 'enc' is followed by 'o', not whitespace. Fully evades the where match().

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS02.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>"C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" -enc:SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQA</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\bwayne</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\OUTLOOK.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\OUTLOOK.EXE"</Data><Data Name='IntegrityLevel'>Medium</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Colon separator (-enc:<base64>) is valid PowerShell syntax; the regex requires \s+ after the switch so it does not match and the event is missed.

findings.detail: The rule requires the DIRECT ParentImage of powershell.exe to be WINWORD/EXCEL/OUTLOOK. The most common real-world maldoc pattern is Office spawning an intermediate (cmd.exe /c, wscript.exe, mshta.exe, or an LOLBin) which then launches powershell -enc. In that chain the powershell EventCode=1 event has ParentImage=cmd.exe (or wscript.exe), so the base search never selects it. attack_step 1 ('Office spawns powershell') is satisfied via a one-hop intermediary and fully evades. No stitching of grandparent (ParentImage lineage / process-tree join on ParentProcessGuid) is done.
findings.fix_hint: Do not require the office binary to be the immediate parent. Correlate on ParentProcessGuid to walk the ancestry, or add a second branch that catches powershell -enc whose grandparent is an Office app, or detect the Office->cmd/wscript/mshta spawn separately.

findings.detail: Image is matched by name only (*\\powershell.exe) and OriginalFileName is never checked. An attacker can Copy-Item the real powershell.exe to any name (e.g. C:\Users\Public\updater.exe) from the macro and run it with -EncodedCommand; it executes identically but Image no longer ends in powershell.exe, so the base filter drops it. pwsh.exe (PowerShell 7), which also accepts -EncodedCommand, is likewise missed. Sysmon populates OriginalFileName='PowerShell.EXE' for all of these but the rule ignores it.
findings.fix_hint: Match on OriginalFileName IN (PowerShell.EXE, pwsh.dll) OR Image="*\\powershell.exe" OR Image="*\\pwsh.exe" instead of relying solely on the on-disk filename.

findings.detail: The ParentImage allowlist is limited to WINWORD/EXCEL/OUTLOOK and omits other macro-capable Office apps that are standard maldoc delivery vectors: POWERPNT.EXE (PowerPoint), MSACCESS.EXE (Access), MSPUB.EXE (Publisher), and VISIO.EXE. A VBA macro in any of these spawning powershell -enc meets the detection intent but is not selected.
findings.fix_hint: Add the remaining Office parents (POWERPNT.EXE, MSACCESS.EXE, MSPUB.EXE, VISIO.EXE, and consider WORDPAD/ONENOTE) to the ParentImage alternation.

findings.detail: hits_per_day is ~0.14 (one event in the 7-day window: WINWORD->powershell by CORP\jdoe) and the stats output never surfaces the decoded base64 or the base64 length distribution, so an analyst cannot quickly distinguish a benign Office add-in/deployment script from a real maldoc. Low volume so not a daily-fire problem, but the single hit is un-triageable from the output as written.
findings.fix_hint: Carry the raw CommandLine, IntegrityLevel, and ideally a base64-decode of the -enc payload into the results to speed triage and reduce manual FP handling.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS01.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='OriginalFileName'>PowerShell.EXE</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>powershell.exe -enc JABzAD0ATgBlAHcALQBPAGIAagBlAGMAdAA=</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='IntegrityLevel'>Medium</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>cmd.exe /c powershell -enc JABzAD0ATgBlAHcALQBPAGIAagBlAGMAdAA=</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Office->cmd->powershell intermediate-parent chain. Macro launched cmd.exe /c which spawned powershell -enc <b64>. The powershell event's ParentImage is cmd.exe, not WINWORD/EXCEL/OUTLOOK, so the base search drops it even though the regex on CommandLine would match. Grandparent lineage is not evaluated.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS01.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Users\Public\updater.exe</Data><Data Name='OriginalFileName'>PowerShell.EXE</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>"C:\Users\Public\updater.exe" -EncodedCommand JABzAD0ATgBlAHcALQBPAGIAagBlAGMAdAA=</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='IntegrityLevel'>Medium</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE" /n</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Renamed-binary evasion. The macro copied powershell.exe to C:\Users\Public\updater.exe and ran it with -EncodedCommand. OriginalFileName still reads PowerShell.EXE but Image does not end in powershell.exe, so Image="*\\powershell.exe" fails and the event is never selected. Detection should key on OriginalFileName.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS02.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='OriginalFileName'>PowerShell.EXE</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>powershell.exe -encodedcommand JABzAD0ATgBlAHcALQBPAGIAagBlAGMAdAA=</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='IntegrityLevel'>Medium</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\POWERPNT.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\POWERPNT.EXE" /n</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Alternate Office parent. A PowerPoint (POWERPNT.EXE) VBA macro directly spawns powershell -encodedcommand <b64>. CommandLine matches the regex and Image matches, but POWERPNT.EXE is not in the WINWORD/EXCEL/OUTLOOK allowlist, so the event is excluded. Same applies to MSACCESS.EXE, MSPUB.EXE, VISIO.EXE.

findings.detail: The renamed-binary / pwsh coverage (OriginalFileName="PowerShell.EXE" OR OriginalFileName="pwsh.dll") rests entirely on the OriginalFileName field, which warnings explicitly flag as 'unverified', and the only provided raw Sysmon EventData block contains NO <Data Name='OriginalFileName'> element at all (only Image, CommandLine, User, ParentImage, ParentCommandLine). If OriginalFileName is not parsed/populated in this index, the base filter collapses to Image="*\powershell.exe" OR Image="*\pwsh.exe" and the copy-and-rename attack (Copy-Item powershell.exe to updater.exe, run with -enc) again fully evades. The prior fix is therefore illusory until OriginalFileName extraction is verified against real EventID 1 data on this host.
findings.fix_hint: Confirm OriginalFileName is extracted (| stats count by OriginalFileName over EventCode=1). If missing, fix the TA/field-alias or fall back to Description/Product/Hashes-based identity; do not rely on a single unverified field for the rename defense.

findings.detail: The intermediary parent allowlist is a fixed, name-only set (cmd|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32). Office->LOLBin->powershell chains that use any other broker are not selected: pcalua.exe, forfiles.exe, wmic.exe, explorer.exe, conhost.exe, schtasks.exe, msbuild.exe, or a renamed copy of cmd.exe. Because the match() anchors on the literal basename, a one-hop broker outside this list satisfies attack_step 1 yet drops out at the 'where match(ParentLower,...)' stage.
findings.fix_hint: Either enumerate the full interpreter/LOLBin set or, better, stitch grandparent lineage via ParentProcessGuid join so any Office ancestor->powershell -enc is caught regardless of the single broker's name.

findings.detail: The in-search exclusion 'where NOT (IntegrityLevel="High" OR IntegrityLevel="System")' is an attacker-satisfiable condition. A maldoc opened by a local-admin user, or a chain that follows a UAC bypass, runs powershell -enc at IntegrityLevel=High and is silently dropped, even though it exactly matches both attack_steps. The exclusion trades a realistic high-integrity maldoc for admin-script noise suppression.
findings.fix_hint: Do not blanket-exclude High integrity for the office_direct ParentType; only de-prioritize, or exclude only when the grandparent/user is a known admin-automation account.

findings.detail: The 'intermediary' branch never verifies that Office (or any maldoc source) is actually in the process lineage - it fires on ANY cmd/cscript/wscript/mshta/rundll32/regsvr32 that spawns powershell with an -enc-style flag at Medium integrity. Enterprise logon scripts, SCCM/GPO deployment, and admin tooling commonly run cscript/cmd -> powershell -EncodedCommand under a non-elevated token, which would alert as ParentType=intermediary with no Office involvement. Current volume is ~0.14/day so not yet daily, but the expanded parent list materially widens benign exposure.
findings.fix_hint: Require an Office ancestor on the intermediary branch (lineage join on ParentProcessGuid), or baseline-exclude known deployment accounts/hosts rather than treating all brokers as malicious.

evasion_events.note: Renamed real powershell.exe copied to updater.exe, launched directly by WINWORD with -enc. Image does not end in powershell.exe/pwsh.exe and this event carries NO OriginalFileName element (matching the provided raw sample), so the base filter drops it entirely despite satisfying both attack_steps.

Office macro brokered through pcalua.exe (Program Compatibility Assistant) instead of cmd/wscript. ParentImage=pcalua.exe is not in the intermediary allowlist, so 'where match(ParentLower,...)' excludes it even though it is a one-hop Office->powershell -enc chain. Same bypass works via forfiles.exe, wmic.exe, explorer.exe, or schtasks.exe.
